paras: The Paradise Alley race riot was a fight between white and Black people in the Paradise alley section of Elkton, Maryland, late on a Saturday night in early August 1905. Pistols and knives were used, several people were badly cut, and seven people were eventually arrested. It is known only from two brief notes in one Eastern Shore weekly, which called it a "race riot."

According to the Democratic Messenger of Snow Hill, "a number of whites and blacks" took part in the riot, which broke out late Saturday night in the part of Elkton known as Paradise alley. The paper's issue of August 12 places that Saturday most likely on August 5, though the date is not stated. "Pistols and knives were freely used," the paper said, and "several were badly cut." Neither the cause of the fighting nor the side that began it is given, and the injured are not named or identified by race.

Five people were arrested soon after the riot, and warrants were issued for several others. Two more arrests followed, of Dallas Wilson and Mary Smith, both described as "colored," bringing the total to seven. The race of the first five arrested is not given, and no report of charges, a hearing or a trial was found.

The Democratic Messenger carried the story twice in its issue of August 12, 1905, in short state-news notes on pages 7 and 2 without headlines or comment. Both notes used the label "race riot" but described the fighting as involving both whites and blacks, and race was attached by name only to the two later arrestees. No other white paper's account was found, and no coverage in the Black press appears in the material searched.
